Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: CIS/RIA Digital ID evaluation (2021) found that neither the ID law nor NIDA law provides rights for data subjects to access, confirm or correct information in the national ID database. Once registered, individuals are not aware of the full content stored. Law No. 058/2021 grants general data subject rights (Art. 20 portability, Art. 19 rectification) but implementation for the ID database is not documented. Value=1 (No formal individual data access mechanism confirmed for the ID database).

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: Rwanda's general court system provides recourse for ID-related grievances through administrative review before NIDA and subsequently administrative courts. The Integrated Electronic Case Management System (IECMS) for judiciary requires NIN authentication. Law No. 058/2021 grants data subjects appeal rights to the supervisory authority (NCSA). However, no ID-specific judicial oversight mechanism exists. Value=2 (Yes but not ID-specific).

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: The NCI-CRVS system (launched Aug 2020) assigns a unique NIN at birth and integrates directly and in real-time with the National Population Registry. Over 600 health facilities, 2,148 cells and 416 sector offices offer real-time birth/death registration linked to NIDA's NPR. Birth registration completeness reached 92.9% in 2022. Value=3 (Full integration).

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: Law No. 029/2023 of 14/06/2023 specifically governs population registration in the National Single Digital Identity System (SDIS). Ministerial Order N° 001/MINICT/24 of 22/01/2024 relates to the Single Digital Identity Coordination Council. Value=2 (Yes).

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Law No. 058/2021 of 13/10/2021 relating to the Protection of Personal Data and Privacy entered into force on 15 October 2021. The National Cyber Security Authority (NCSA) is the designated supervisory authority. Value=2 (Yes).

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: Law No. 058/2021 designates the National Cyber Security Authority (NCSA) as the supervisory authority with powers to oversee implementation, issue registration certificates to data controllers/processors, and impose administrative sanctions. Value=2 (Yes).

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: Law No. 14/2008 makes possession and carrying of the national identity card obligatory for every Rwandan aged 16 and above. The NIN/National ID is the primary legal proof of identity accepted for healthcare, higher education, taxation, pensions, social assistance, financial services, and travel within EAC (Kenya, Uganda). Value=2 (Yes).

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: Rwanda has a comprehensive legal framework: Law No. 14/2008 (amended 2018) governing national ID; Law No. 43/2011 establishing NIDA; Law No. 029/2023 governing population registration in the Single Digital Identity System; and Law No. 058/2021 on Data Protection and Privacy. Value=2 (Yes).

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: Rwanda's National Population Registry (NPR) and NID database have been fully digital since 2008 following the door-to-door census and biometric capture campaign. No paper-only records for the current system; the new SDIS is 100% digital. Value=3 (Digital).

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: Current law (Law No. 14/2008, amended 2018) mandates ID at age 16. The new SDIS (Law No. 029/2023) extends enrollment to include newborns at birth via the CRVS-linked NPR system, with physical card issuance beginning at 16. Children under 5 receive a photograph during SDIS enrollment. NIDA stated the new digital ID 'will be issued from birth.' The NPR captures children below 16. For the national ID card (credential), eligibility remains 16+. Value=1 (>17 for credential; enrollment at birth for the registry is a transition in progress).

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: Law No. 14/2008 states: 'Possession of and carrying the national identity card is obligatory to every Rwandan aged sixteen (16) and above.' Enrollment and possession are mandatory for all eligible Rwandans. Value=3 (Mandatory for all).

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: National ID is required for Community-Based Health Insurance (CBHI/Mutuelle de Santé) enrollment and healthcare access. World Bank report confirms NID is required for 'healthcare.' SDIS is designed to improve healthcare service delivery. Birth registration via NCI-CRVS issues NIN at birth for healthcare purposes. Value=3 (Mandatory).

Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: NIDA estimates >98% of the eligible population (16+) have been issued a national ID card. The NPR captures approximately 98% of the total population. World Bank People's Perspectives report (2021) confirms this figure. Value=5 (>89%).

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: National ID is mandatory for accessing social protection services. The Ubudehe social register is linked to the NIN for targeting safety net programs. Rwanda Social Security Board (RSSB) uses NIN. World Bank report confirms NID is required for 'social assistance' and government services. Value=3 (Mandatory).
